papers.title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
papers.abstract: Sinusoidal blade pitching can improve vertical-axis turbine performance, but whether a blade could follow the same motion passively depends on the energy exchanged through pitching. This study experimentally examines 480 prescribed-pitch conditions using a single-blade model following a circular trajectory in a water channel at four tip-speed ratios (TSRs) from 1.25 to 3.14. The amplitude associated with the highest measured power decreases from 16° to 12° and then 8° as TSR increases, with the corresponding phase shifting from 0 to pi/4. At TSRs of 1.25 and 3.14, the cycle-averaged power coefficient increases from 0.0047 to 0.1037 and from 0.4698 to 0.5948, respectively. Pitching-energy maps show nearly neutral net hydrodynamic pitching work for the highest-performing motions at the two lower TSRs and net energy transfer from the flow to pitching at the two higher TSRs. Virtual damping narrows the positive-energy region, although the higher-TSR best-tested motions retain an energy surplus at nonzero damping. However, net energy transfer from the flow to pitching also occurs for motions with substantial power losses. At the lowest TSR, phase-resolved force measurements and particle image velocimetry link the gain to delayed dynamic-stall-vortex formation and shedding, prolonged favorable loading, and reduced subsequent negative power. At the highest TSR, the flow and loading change locally, with little alteration of the main power-producing event. The joint maps identify performance-enhancing motions with an energetic margin against assumed dissipation, providing candidates for further passive or assisted pitching studies.

papers.title: Augmentation of cardiovascular flow measurements with generative diffusion models
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular imaging offers several ways to measure blood flow, but each provides an incomplete, resolution-limited, or noisy view of the underlying dynamics. Reconstructing the missing information is inherently ambiguous because several flow fields may be compatible with the same observation. Here, we investigate generative diffusion models as tools for cardiovascular-flow generation and reconstruction using a fully controlled state-of-the-art dataset from a digital twin of a healthy human left heart. First, we show how unconditional samples reproduce the changing anatomy and the highly fluctuating statistical properties of the flow throughout the cardiac cycle. Second, we test the conditional inference of our generative model by reconstructing an entire 2D planar section of geometry and flow configurations from a limited portion. Repeated reconstructions allow us to represent a range of plausible completions, going beyond a single deterministic estimate, while their mean retains the principal features of the reference flow. Comparison with a Gaussian process regression baseline on the same reduced domain highlights the main advantage of diffusion models: their reconstructed ensembles capture a broader range of velocity and gradient fluctuations, better encompassing ground-truth features that the baseline distributions can miss. Our results provide a quantitative proof of concept for probabilistic reconstruction of incomplete cardiovascular-flow measurements and demonstrate the potential for groundbreaking applications to the augmentation of in-vivo cardiovascular imaging data.

papers.title: Impulsive ejection of Worthington jets by flow focusing. Influence of a soluble surfactant
papers.abstract: We experimentally investigate impulsive Worthington jet generation by flow focusing, considering the liquid meniscus location that maximizes the flow-focusing effect. This effect increases the jet velocity by up to two orders of magnitude over the bottom liquid velocity after impact. At sufficiently high liquid velocities, jet formation is governed primarily by inertia, making jet velocity largely independent of liquid viscosity, surface tension, and surfactant effects. Each liquid exhibits an optimum impact velocity that maximizes momentum transfer. Surfynol 465 lowers the impactvelocity threshold for water-jet emission and increases jet velocity by rapidly restoring equilibrium surface tension. In contrast, Triton X-100 has an almost negligible effect because of its slower adsorption kinetics. Importantly, both surfactants reduce jet diameter and, consequently, droplet size. This reduction is particularly significant with Surfynol 465 at high impact velocities, suggesting potential applications, for instance, in high-resolution printing technologies. The jet loaded with Surfynol 465 was even faster than that of the glycerine-water mixture with the same Ohnesorge and Weber numbers. This suggests that adding Surfynol 465 further accelerates jet emission, exceeding the speed attained by a clean interface with the same reduced equilibrium surface tension.

papers.title: Ultrasensitive measurement of phase dynamics by time-holographic dark-port readout of a marginally imbalanced interferometer
papers.abstract: Resolving displacements and surface irregularities far below a nanometer is now indispensable across fields, from precision manufacturing and biotechnology to nanoscience and fundamental metrology. High-precision optical interferometry reaches this $λ/1{,}000$ regime by reading out optical power, which provides a smooth response over the measurement range. Here we instead read out the complex dark-port field of a marginally imbalanced interferometer, whose phase response to small internal phase deviations $φ_{\textrm{in}}$ near destructive interference becomes extremely steep. For a small arm-amplitude imbalance $μ$, the tangent $T_{\textrm{out}}$ of the dark-port phase reduces to $μ^{-1}φ_{\textrm{in}}$, defining a phase magnification $M=μ^{-1}$. Crucially, this tangent estimator stays linear over a range $|φ_{\textrm{in}}|\lesssim\sqrt{|μ|}$---much larger than the imbalance $|μ|$ itself for $|μ|\ll1$---so that fine temporal substructure is resolved within much larger phase excursions. $T_{\textrm{out}}$ is synthesized from the dark-port complex field by optical time-domain holography and Fourier demodulation---a heterodyne readout that is intrinsically immune to laser relative-intensity noise at any magnification, and gives time-resolved access to phase dynamics. In a proof-of-principle Mach--Zehnder experiment, without optimization or environmental isolation, we demonstrate $|M|>10^3$ and optical-path resolution better than $λ/100{,}000$ ($\approx5~\textrm{pm}$), with a shot-noise floor orders of magnitude below this environment-limited value. The approach is compact, tunable, and compatible with existing interferometric platforms, offering a practical route to enhanced phase sensitivity in metrology, sensing, and optical instrumentation.

papers.title: Closed-loop policy optimisation for cylinder wake control via differentiable simulation
papers.abstract: Suppressing vortex shedding behind a circular cylinder is a classical problem in active flow control.Model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL) learns such policies by interacting with the flow without differentiating its dynamics, which typically requires a large interaction budget. This study optimises closed-loop policies by differentiable simulation: control-loss gradients propagate through the simulated flow to the policy parameters, which are updated by reverse-mode automatic differentiation. The policy maps local velocity measurements to a jet amplitude imposed through differentiable synthetic-jet boundary conditions. In a two-dimensional confined cylinder wake at Rey=100, eight policy updates (about 78 shedding periods of forward simulation) give approximately 8% drag reduction and 99.6% suppression of lift fluctuations, the drag level being comparable to reported DRL results. Suppression is sustained by feedback: a mean-matched constant jet does not maintain it, whereas the same policy responds similarly at three activation phases and recovers after upstream disturbances. A velocity-deviation reward alone retains strong suppression, and observations of two instantaneous velocity components at one near-wake or surface location reach about 99.8% suppression, whereas a single surface pressure leaves residual oscillations. Together with related DRL results, this suggests that reward and observation requirements here are set by policy optimisation and flow physics.

papers.title: Forbidden T-symmetry breaking in time-dependent non-Hermitian systems with gain and loss
papers.abstract: Parity-time ($PT$) symmetry has attracted significant interest in photonics and related fields in recent years. With sufficiently weak gain and loss, these systems typically exhibit entirely real energy levels, with all corresponding wave functions remaining $PT$ symmetric. As the strength of gain and loss increases, complex-conjugate energy levels are expected to emerge, signaling the onset of $PT$ symmetry breaking. Similar properties can be found in non-Hermitian systems with other antilinear symmetries as well, where parity is replaced by another operator such as rotation ($R$) or simply the identity operator, resulting in $RT$-symmetric and $T$-symmetric non-Hermitian systems. In this work, we demonstrate that this typical scenario of non-Hermitian symmetry breaking in a finite Hilbert space is forbidden in a class of time-dependent systems with gain and loss and $T$ symmetry: the system remains in its $T$-symmetric phase as we increase the strength of gain and loss, even when the spatial distribution of gain and loss is random. Furthermore, this behavior is also independent of the duration or period of the temporal modulation. In contrast, this forbidden non-Hermitian symmetry breaking does not occur when the same systems are modified to display $PT$ symmetry instead. Our findings highlight contrasting behaviors in time-dependent and time-independent non-Hermitian systems, creating new possibilities and opportunities for future investigations.

papers.title: A new restitution model for wet particle collisions using fully resolved numerical simulations
papers.abstract: Particle collisions play a central role in wet particle processes such as granulation, drying, and chemical reactors, yet the influence of the liquid on the collision dynamics remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates the influence of liquid viscosity, liquid density, liquid content, impact velocity, solid density, and surface tension on the wet restitution coefficient using numerical simulations. In this study, a Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) framework is used that has been validated against dedicated experiments of wet-wet particle collisions, showing a good agreement for both liquid-bridge evolution and rebound dynamics. The restitution coefficient decreases with increasing liquid viscosity, liquid density, and liquid-to-solid density ratio, whereas increasing impact velocity increases rebound. The negligible influence of surface tension indicates that viscous dissipation is the dominant source of energy loss under the investigated conditions. As existing Stokes number formulations were found to only capture part of the governing physics, a generalized Stokes number is proposed to incorporate both the viscous and inertial response time scales. A modified restitution coefficient model based on the generalized Stokes number successfully collapses the numerical and experimental data onto a single trend and predicts the wet restitution coefficient with an RMSE of only 4.99%.

papers.title: Lacrymaria-like dynamics: compression and length change in active slender bodies
papers.abstract: Length change is central to the behaviour of many active slender bodies, yet most elastohydrodynamic models of microscopic locomotion treat filaments as effectively inextensible. Here we introduce a compressible $N$-link formulation for planar active filaments, in which both bending angles and segment lengths are dynamical variables coupled through local hydrodynamic drag, modelled using resistive force theory. We first use the model to test whether passive extensibility can improve bending-driven swimming and crawling. Across the parameter ranges studied, passive compressibility usually reduces locomotion speed, indicating that axial compliance alone is not a robust mechanism for propulsion enhancement. We then prescribe active rest-length waves and show that compression can either enhance, suppress, or redirect locomotion depending on its phase, wavelength, and frequency relative to bending. Finally, motivated by the extensible neck dynamics of \textit{Lacrymaria olor}, we apply the method to clamped and free filaments driven by oscillatory follower forces. These examples show that elastic compression-bending coupling can reorganise swimming, exploration, and locomotion in strongly deforming active filaments.

papers.title: A sliding mode observer perspective on chaos synchronisation of turbulent flows
papers.abstract: State estimation of turbulent flows is challenging as infinitesimal prediction errors grow exponentially due to chaos. However, when signals from one chaotic system (the master) are injected into an identical system with different initial conditions (the slave), the slave can synchronise with the master --- a phenomenon observed in turbulent flows. From a control-theoretic perspective, this synchronisation problem can be viewed as observer design. We first show that synchronisation by direct substitution of observed variables into the slave system is equivalent to a sliding mode observer. This perspective enables the analytical verification of stability as well as the design of feedback for robustness. We focus on reduced-order Navier--Stokes models with quadratic non-linearities, a broad class of systems for which stability can be analysed by seeking Lyapunov functions through parameter-dependent linear matrix inequalities solved via semidefinite programming. Extending this framework, we develop a neural network approach combining a neural ordinary differential equation with a decoder to learn data-driven mappings from observation histories to companion forms, where observer design is greatly simplified. Results are demonstrated on the Lorenz system and a nine-dimensional reduced order model of a turbulent shear flow. This work opens opportunities in the rigorous development of observers for turbulent flows.

papers.title: Regular reflection of shock waves: non-equilibrium effects for various steady flow parameters
papers.abstract: A parametric study of the non-equilibrium region formed by the steady regular reflection of two symmetric oblique shock waves in a monatomic gas is performed using the direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method. Three series of calculations are considered, with the incident-shock normal Mach number fixed at 2, 4 and 8, respectively. Within each series, the incidence angle is reduced while the normal strength of the incident shock remains unchanged. The decrease in angle primarily results in a longer non-equilibrium region of shock-wave interaction. Over the parameter range considered, the density-transition width along the plane of symmetry is approximately inversely proportional to the sine of the incidence angle. Increasing the normal Mach number enhances temperature anisotropy, the local temperature overshoot relative to the equilibrium downstream state, and the streamwise-velocity undershoot.

papers.title: Adaptive-Optics-Aware Uplink and Downlink Analysis of Ground-to-HAPS FSO Links
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present an adaptive optics (AO)-aware analytical framework for ground-to- high-altitude platform station (HAPS) free-space optical (FSO) links considering both uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) transmission. The proposed model combines atmospheric attenuation, Exponentiated Weibull (EW) turbulence, Beckmann-type pointing error (PE), and field-of-view (FoV)-limited angle-of-arrival (AOA) loss. Adaptive optics correction (AOC) is incorporated through the number of corrected modes, allowing the impact of partial and stronger wavefront compensation to be directly reflected in the channel statistics. Analytical and numerically tractable expressions are derived for the outage probability (OP), average bit-error rate (BER), and an ergodic achievable-rate lower bound (EALB) optical channel. High signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) approximations are also developed, showing that AOA/FoV blocking introduces irreducible OP and BER floors, while the decaying nonblocked component is governed by the small-channel-gain behavior of the turbulence and PE distributions. Numerical results demonstrate that the DL generally outperforms the UL because of the direction-dependent interaction with near-ground turbulence. The results also show that increasing the number of AOC modes improves OP, BER, and the EALB, although the improvement gradually saturates. The effects of average SNR, HAPS altitude, zenith angle, beam waist, boresight error, and receiver FoV are further investigated to provide practical design insight for AO-assisted ground-to-HAPS FSO systems.

papers.title: Actively stabilized Fabry-Pérot notch filters for correlated photons from cold two-level atoms
papers.abstract: We report two actively stabilized Fabry-Pérot cavities operated as reflection-mode notch filters for biphotons generated by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a cold two-level atomic ensemble. In this source, elastic scattering at the excitation frequency increases the single-detector count rates and the accidental-coincidence background, thereby limiting the observed nonclassical correlations. One cavity is placed in each photon-collection mode. An acousto-optic modulator frequency-dithers an auxiliary field, and synchronous demodulation of the transmitted power provides the locking discriminator. Light resonant with the auxiliary field is transmitted, whereas the detuned components are reflected toward the photon detectors. By tuning the auxiliary field to the same frequency as the excitation field, we filter these components and direct a larger portion of the quantum-correlated sidebands to the detection. The cavities have linewidths of approximately 2 MHz and remain locked for longer than a typical correlation acquisition. The measured Cauchy-Schwarz parameter exceeds unity in both configurations, with a higher central value with filtering ($\overline{R} = 4.15 \pm 0.93$) than without ($\overline{R} = 2.33 \pm 0.20$). This architecture provides actively stabilized rejection of a narrow spectral interval, simultaneously, for two fields detected in different directions. Filter performance could be further improved by adjusting the cavity linewidth to better match the spectral width of the central component and by reducing losses in the filters.

papers.title: Emergent Fourfold Symmetry in Polarization Images: Local Origin and Diffractive Breakdown
papers.abstract: A polarization image can gain or lose rotational symmetry with no change in material symmetry. In axisymmetric anisotropic systems, covariance restricts the field to azimuthal orders $m=0,\pm2$, guaranteeing twofold but not fourfold symmetry; pointwise unitarity adds fourfold symmetry, which diffraction can destroy. Holographic Jones fields of liquid-crystal torons show propagation shifts the twofold--fourfold balance; for the same director, a marching-wave model qualitatively reproduces the twofold morphology missed by a local model. This establishes a symmetry hierarchy for polarization imaging.

papers.title: Single-shot holographic gradients for training wavefronts through disorder
papers.abstract: Training optical systems in situ needs the gradient of their loss, yet a camera records only intensity and the medium is never exactly known. We show that one off-axis hologram gives this gradient, an approach we call holographic gradients. Light passes through the medium only forward; the hologram measures the error, and a compact adjoint, fitted to ten probes, is refreshed in seconds during train- ing. Each step costs one modulated pattern. Through a thin diffuser, it focuses light and forms images as well as a measured transmission matrix, without its thousands of patterns. Under controlled drift, refreshing the adjoint recovers a grating to 17.6 dB, against 9.1 dB for a frozen model and 19.5 dB without drift, and training succeeds through a thick diffuser. Trained offline, the reference beam becomes a computing layer that plays a video game. Holographic gradients let optical systems learn while they operate, from imaging through dynamic media to self-correcting processors.

papers.title: How Meandering Flow Sculpts Ice
papers.abstract: Ice-water phase change subject to a mean flow widely exists in the Cryosphere, with implications on glacier evolution, human transportation, flooding events, etc. Understanding the relevant phase change dynamics requires identifying the roles of shear and rotation due to the mean flow. Combining experiments, numerical simulations and theoretical modelling, we reveal the combined effects of shear and rotation on the coupled dynamics of water flow, heat transfer and phase change in an annular system. Increasing shear and rotation drive a stronger secondary circulation which significantly enhances global heat transfer and redistributes the radial heat flux, and eventually lead to a thinner equilibrium ice layer and a larger ice thickness difference in the radial direction. Further, we develop an integral thermal balance model that explains the mean ice thickness through estimating the additional heat transfer, and a local thermal balance model that explains the inner-outer ice thickness difference by relating it to the non-uniform convective heat flux. The local model shows qualitative agreement with field measurements when applied to an ice-covered meandering river. These results contribute to understanding the common physical mechanism for ice-water phase change under shear and rotation, offering a theoretical basis for explaining and predicting ice evolution in meandering rivers among other relevant scenarios.

papers.title: A 3D PINN-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Pulmonary Hemodynamics Using Windkessel Models
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular fluid dynamics modeling relies heavily on mesh-based numerical methods such as Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). While accurate, these methods entail significant computational costs and complex meshing workflows that limit their translation to clinical practice. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) are a promising meshless alternative that embeds the governing equations directly into neural network training. In this work, we propose a PINN framework for pulsatile blood flow in patient-specific geometries with dynamic lumped-parameter Windkessel (RCR) outlet conditions representing distal vascular impedance. Coupling the Windkessel ODE to a 3D network raises two difficulties: the ODE alone does not fix the pressure level, and the local pressure variations that drive the flow are orders of magnitude smaller than the basal pressure imposed by the outlet. We address them by decomposing pressure into a time-dependent basal part and a spatially varying part, an initial condition and gauge for the Windkessel equation, a global mass-balance constraint, and a periodic Fourier embedding of time. Validated on 2D canonical channels (steady and pulsatile, with and without RCR outlet), the framework is then applied to a patient-specific right pulmonary artery, reproducing outlet flow, mean pressure, and the velocity and dynamic pressure fields with errors on the order of the data resolution. Finally, we solve the inverse problem of identifying the three Windkessel parameters of the outlet from synthetic data, recovering them with errors of about 0.3% from deliberately wrong initial values. Residual biases in the local pressure field and the need to test robustness to noisy clinical data remain open, but the results support PINNs as complementary tools for meshless hemodynamics and patient-specific digital twins.

papers.title: Monolithic ultraviolet-to- near infrared photodetection enabled by an aluminium oxide photonic platform
papers.abstract: Broadband photonic integrated circuits require waveguide platforms that combine low optical loss across a wide spectral range with integrated photodetection. Here we demonstrate a monolithically integrated atomic-layer-deposited (ALD) aluminium oxide (Al$_2$O$_3$)-on-silicon platform enabling waveguide-coupled photodetection from the ultraviolet to the near-infrared. The architecture employs evanescent coupling between low-loss Al$_2$O$_3$ waveguides and silicon p-i-n photodiodes. The platform supports photodetection at 375, 658 and 780 nm, extending integrated silicon photodetection into the ultraviolet. The devices exhibit linear photocurrent scaling with optical power, dark currents of approximately 2 pA at 50 V reverse bias and nanosecond-scale temporal response. We further demonstrate centimetre-scale ultraviolet Mach-Zehnder interferometer circuits with integrated photodiodes. The same detector architecture is implemented with Si$_3$N$_4$ waveguides, whereas the lower ultraviolet propagation loss of Al$_2$O$_3$ enables an approximately 15-fold higher photodetection response at 375 nm. These results establish ALD Al$_2$O$_3$ as a broadband integrated photonics platform for sensing, spectroscopy and quantum technologies.

papers.title: 60-cm-long In-vacuum Zerodur Optical Cavity for Optical Lattice Atom Interferometry
papers.abstract: Optical cavities are widely used in atomic physics experiments to control the spatial geometry and spectral properties of atom-light interactions. Recently, an optical lattice generated by the pristine mode of an optical cavity was utilized to hold and extend the quantum coherence of atomic spatial superpositions. Here, we describe an in-vacuum optical cavity designed to enhance the spatial and temporal coherence of optical lattice atom interferometers to one millimeter wavepacket separations and one minute measurement durations. The cavity uses a rigid Zerodur spacer to suppress the negative effects of thermal drift and mechanical-acoustic vibrations on the atomic motional state. The 60 cm-long cavity spacer provides ample optical access for the laser beams and imaging optics necessary for the preparation, quantum control, and read-out of the atomic state, as well as room for various source mass configurations for localized gravitational measurements. An integrated differential pumping structure enables compatibility with ultrahigh-vacuum operation and optical interferometry allows for in-situ vibration monitoring. The performance of the optical cavity is methodically characterized: we measure mirror vibration noise with amplitude below 5 nm/$\sqrt{\rm Hz}$ in a wide frequency range of 2 Hz - 100 kHz and a slow 15 MHz thermal drift of the cavity resonance over 47 hours, which can be readily stabilized with an integrated piezo. The optical cavity supports both 852-nm light for Raman transitions and 1064-nm light for the optical lattice, with a free spectral range matched to an integer divisor of the cesium ground-state hyperfine splitting.

papers.title: Composite Dielectric-Loaded Metallic Metagratings for Dual-Polarized Transmissive Beam Manipulation
papers.abstract: We present and experimentally demonstrate a comprehensive analytical suite for the design of transmissive metal-based metagratings (MGs) for dual-polarized anomalous refraction. Considering a composite configuration of perforated metallic slabs with controlled dielectric loading, we develop a rigorous mode-matching formulation tying the various MG degrees of freedom to the various reflected and transmitted Floquet-Bloch modes, enabling efficient beam deflection for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarizations. Inherently versatile, the analytical framework accurately models single-layer and double-layer constructs with multiple rectangular perforations per unit cell, each potentially loaded with dielectric material. We harness this degree-of-freedom abundance to devise diverse polarization-sensitive transmissive MGs, ranging from all-metallic single-layer and double-layer structures for single-polarized (TM or TE) perfect anomalous refraction, to dielectric-loaded architectures implementing dual-polarized routing of the incident wave. Beyond highlighting concrete paths to address TE-polarized fields in such formations, our results, validated via full-wave simulations and experiments at K band, showcase the great potential of metal-based MGs for manipulating fields in transmission, facilitating effective synthesis of durable dual-polarized beamforming superstrates for environmentally demanding and high power antenna applications.

papers.title: Development and control of Görtler vortices in the SD-2 serpentine diffuser
papers.abstract: This study investigates and controls the flow through a serpentine diffuser using wall-modeled large-eddy simulations (WMLES), with emphasis on the formation of streamwise vortices, their contribution to flow distortion, and their suppression using opposition control. Following Agrawal et al., AIAA Journal (2026), simulations are performed at three Mach numbers, $Ma_{AIP} =0.36, 0.46,0.54$. Adverse pressure gradients and centrifugal forces induced by geometric features of the diffuser promote flow separation and lead to the formation of counter-rotating Görtler vortices. Downstream of the second bend, the transition from an elliptical to a circular cross-section drives these vortices toward the centerline along the spanwise direction, ejecting low-momentum fluid from the near-wall region into the core. A steady opposition-control strategy using wall-normal velocity forcing is employed to attenuate the streamwise vortices. The control strategy increases pressure recovery, reduces flow distortion, and substantially suppresses total-pressure fluctuations across all three Mach numbers. The maximum flow distortion is reduced by $\approx 50\%$ at the two lower Mach numbers and by $34\%$ at $Ma_{AIP}=0.54$. The variance of the total-pressure fluctuations is reduced by approximately two orders of magnitude near the center of the AIP and by a factor of two near the periphery. An input-output power analysis further shows a net positive power gain at all three Mach numbers, with a maximum control efficiency of approximately $65\%$ at the lowest Mach number, although the power efficiency decreases significantly at higher Mach numbers due to the larger actuation amplitudes required.

papers.title: Hamiltonian symmetry behind the vanishing of four-wave interactions at non-trivial resonances for one-dimensional deep-water waves
papers.abstract: The unexpected cancellation of non-trivial resonant four-wave interactions is the foundation of several compact and accurate models for one-dimensional deep-water waves. The reasons for this cancellation are not yet fully understood. An additional integral of motion would account for it, but to our knowledge no corresponding symmetry has been identified. Here it is shown that in real canonical variables with the cubic terms eliminated, the fourth-order Hamiltonian is invariant under a sign-dependent phase rotation generated by the Hilbert transform. The corresponding Noether charge is the action imbalance between right- and left-moving waves, conserved exactly although number-changing quartic terms remain. The symmetry confines the quartic kernel to the sector with two wavenumbers of each sign, which contains no non-trivial resonance, so the cancellation follows without calculation. In complex normal variables the symmetry is the vanishing of the reduced Zakharov kernel whenever the product of the four wavenumbers is non-positive, and the known closed form of that kernel follows directly. The symmetry is the fourth-order instance of a selection rule valid at every order in these variables: no term of the Hamiltonian has a single wavenumber of the minority sign. The rule rests on the holomorphic structure of planar deep-water flow and on its square-root dispersion relation.

papers.title: Efficient convolution-based nonparaxial propagation of partially coherent light
papers.abstract: We derive an efficient formulation for wide-angle propagation of partially coherent light from extended incoherent sources, extending the generalized van Cittert-Zernike Schell (GVS) propagator beyond the paraxial regime with absolute radiometric normalization. Within the Fresnel model, we establish that GVS and the classical paraxial source-PSF convolution are algebraically equivalent, explicitly deriving the corresponding source inversion, magnification, and absolute radiometric normalization. The resulting separation of mapped source and coherent pupil response enables wide-angle convolution in direction-cosine coordinates. Within a physically motivated diffracted-radiance formulation, this far-field convolution is exact for incoherent plane-wave mixtures. The same power prescription also relates delta-correlated source statistics to Lambertian radiance and hemispherical emitted power. At finite distances, we use a common incident curvature and approximate the source contributions by shifting and weighting a single coherent monitor response in direction-cosine coordinates. The differentiable formulation supports gradient-based inverse design of diffractive elements and metasurfaces represented by scalar pupils. Examples reveal geometric distortion and irradiance fall-off missed by the paraxial models and demonstrate wide-angle beam shaping at finite distances. A benchmark shows orders of magnitude faster evaluation than source-by-source propagation with a common error tolerance.

papers.title: Probabilistic image generation conditioned on an optical latent code
papers.abstract: While diffractive optical networks compress images into compact representations, such measurements have predominantly served discriminative inference or deterministic reconstruction. Here we demonstrate probabilistic image generation conditioned solely on a 16_bit binary optical latent code (OLC) formed by a diffractive encoder and binarized camera readout. The intentionally many-to-one mapping makes each OLC specify a class of OLC-compatible images rather than a unique reconstruction target. An OLC_conditioned conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) learns this distribution, while optical re-encoding promotes consistency between generated images and the measured OLC. Numerical characterization and proof-of-concept acquisition with a spatial light modulator_camera system establish the OLC as a physically accessible generative condition. On MNIST, samples generated from a single OLC vary in morphology while preserving class identity, and their optical-recognition accuracy reaches 81.6%, close to the 81.9% obtained from the source OLCs. These results link compact optical sensing to probabilistic synthesis of optically recognizable images.

papers.title: Unconventional Photon Blockade in Second-Order Nonlinearity Coupled Cavities with Asymmetric Dissipation
papers.abstract: We investigate the unconventional photon blockade in a second-order nonlinearity coupled double-cavity system with asymmetric dissipation. By treating the cavity decay rates as independent parameters, we analytically derive two exact families of optimal blockade conditions. While the first family recovers and generalizes the symmetric-dissipation results of previous studies, the second family, arising uniquely from an asymmetric dissipation ratio of $κ_B = 2κ_A$, completely locks the relative phase of the interference pathways. Importantly, we find that this asymmetric dissipation not only renders the optimal blockade condition strictly immune to frequency detuning, but also enhances the blockade depth by an order of magnitude compared to the resonant case. Furthermore, the mean photon number remains almost unaffected, proving that this enhanced robustness is achieved without sacrificing the brightness of the single-photon source. These findings offer a promising route toward robust single-photon generation in passive cavities with second-order nonlinearity.

papers.title: Power Law Transients in Perovskite Photoluminescence
papers.abstract: Carrier dynamics and recombination in perovskite thin films are often explored through transient photoluminescence (PL) measurements and subsequent analysis based on single/multi-exponentials. In contrast, here we show that several experimental PL transients reported in literature vary as power laws with time and are not multi-exponentials. Puzzlingly, the existing theoretical methods are ill-equipped to explain the origin and implications of such power law trends. Our analysis resolves this puzzle and correlates the power law exponents with the trap distributions. Curiously, we show that PL transients could vary as $t^{-2}$ even in the presence of dominant monomolecular recombination while the existing theory associates this unique trend exclusively with dominant bimolecular recombination. These findings identify the limits of applicability of concepts such as differential lifetime and highlight the need for predictive modeling synergistic with insightful data analysis towards performance optimization of perovskite optoelectronic devices.

papers.title: Shear thinning confines the wall forcing: laminar chaotic mixing of Carreau fluids in a rotating arc-wall mixer
papers.abstract: With two-dimensional simulations of Carreau fluids of power-law index $N$ from 1 to 0.4, I study how shear thinning modifies laminar chaotic mixing in an open channel stirred by three arc-shaped wall segments rotating back and forth periodically, the upper one in anti-phase with the two lower ones. The outlet mixing efficiency falls monotonically, by 14 percent from $N=1$ to 0.4, mostly between $N=0.85$ and 0.6. The bulk flow and its chaotic saddle are nearly unaffected. Shear thinning acts instead through a thin layer of reduced viscosity around the moving arcs: the geometric penetration length of the wall forcing shortens as the 0.3 power of the time-mean wall viscosity, within 4 percent over a fourfold range of forcing. This confinement weakens the stretching, and the penetration length predicts the mixing efficiency ($r^2=0.97$). The optimal Strouhal number stays close to 0.7 for all fluids, but shear thinning narrows the range of efficient periods. A lamellar model indicates that the relative penalty of shear thinning grows with the Peclet number. As the injected power scales with the wall viscosity, the mixing efficiency per unit energy rises 2.6-fold from $N=1$ to 0.4, and at equal energy per unit volume, with a faster rotation, the fluid with $N=0.4$ mixes as well as the Newtonian one, and better at larger energies. In wall-driven mixers, the reach of the forcing, not the bulk viscosity, is the quantity to control.

papers.title: Droplet formation dynamics in a T-junction via pulsed electrohydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Numerical simulations based on the phase-field lattice Boltzmann method are employed to investigate droplet formation dynamics in a T-junction microchannel under pulsed electrohydrodynamics. The applied electric field modulates the interfacial morphology, thereby altering the hydrodynamic stress distribution acting on the liquid-liquid interface. Three configurations are examined: no electric field, top-biased electrode, and bottom-biased electrode. The results show that the top-biased electrode promotes rapid transverse migration of the dispersed phase towards the upper wall, thereby accelerating the transition to the channel-blocking stage. By contrast, under the bottom-biased electrode, the dispersed phase first adheres to the lower wall and subsequently deforms upward under the electric force. As a result, the droplet formation dynamics are strongly affected by the spatial distribution of the electric field. The droplet generation process is further divided into a filling stage and a squeezing stage based on theoretical analysis. During the filling stage, the electric force modifies the filling duration but has little influence on the filling flux. During the squeezing stage, the necking rate and breakup time are governed by the pinning of the dispersed-phase contact line on the channel wall. Compared with constant electric forcing, pulsed electric forcing introduces an additional temporal degree of freedom, enabling stage-dependent modulation of interfacial evolution and breakup dynamics. Finally, droplet sequence diagrams and regime maps are presented for different pulse parameters. The results demonstrate that pulsed electrohydrodynamics in a T-junction enables active and programmable control of consecutive droplet generation.

papers.title: Galvanometer Mirror Based Femtosecond-Laser Volumetric Displays
papers.abstract: Femtosecond-laser-induced plasma enables self-emissive voxels to be generated directly in air for drawing three-dimensional images. Galvanometer-mirror-based beam scanning provides a method for rapidly moving plasma voxels using a relatively simple optical configuration. However, the generated plasma voxels are not ideal points but luminous regions with finite lengths and widths. Variations in voxel shape and orientation caused by focusing and scanning conditions may therefore affect the appearance of rendered points and lines. Nevertheless, quantitative relationships between focusing and scanning conditions and plasma-voxel geometry remain insufficiently characterized in systems using a two-axis galvanometer mirror and a single focusing lens. Here, we quantitatively investigate how focal length and two-axis galvanometer scan angle affect the shape of plasma voxels and the projected inclination of their principal axes. For focal lengths ranging from 75 to 300 mm, the mean plasma length increased from 1.39 to 4.64 mm. These results indicate that increasing the focal length produces more elongated and anisotropic plasma voxels. The projected inclination of the plasma principal axis varied approximately linearly with the corresponding scan angle, although the response differed between the two scanning axes. These results provide quantitative design data for selecting focusing conditions and correcting voxel shape and orientation according to scanning conditions in galvanometer-mirror-based aerial volumetric displays.

papers.title: Benchmarking Quantum Key Distribution Hardware Across Operating Conditions
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is entering national fibre networks, but published secret key rates (SKRs) are measured over different distances, wavelengths, classical traffic loads and clock rates, so systems are hard to compare. We write the SKR as the product of the transmitter clock rate, the channel transmittance and the secret key per received pulse. This third factor, the noise-normalised key rate (NNKR), needs four commonly reported parameters and depends mainly on the equipment wherever the SKR is proportional to transmittance. A companion metric, the implementation efficiency (IE), compares the SKR with the ideal key rate of its channel, including classical-traffic noise. For fixed loss-limited equipment, NNKR is independent of channel loss, whereas the fraction of the repeaterless bound varies 1.6-fold over 2-25 dB. An analytic model relates the flat loss range of NNKR to the detector noise count rate and dead time. We apply both metrics to ten published coexistence experiments, and NNKR to 42,115 measurements from four systems of two vendors and four high-rate laboratory systems. For one production system, NNKR has a 6.9% coefficient of variation over 17 dB of attenuation and agrees within 0.7 dB with three of four published deployments of that platform. Under coexistence, that platform's NNKR and IE stay within 0.5 dB of their standalone values. In decibels, NNKR is a sum of component penalties, as in an optical link budget, and for one laboratory system the budget from its published parameters and measured secure fraction closes within 0.3 dB.

papers.title: Spatially multiplexed opto-electronic Ising machine with single-shot parallel readout of 100,000 spins
papers.abstract: Ising machines offer a promising route to solving NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems by mapping them onto the ground state of the Ising model. Free-space optical implementations are attractive for their inherent parallelism, scalability, and energy efficiency, yet nearly all rely on individual, sequential spin updates, leaving most of this parallelism unexploited. Here, we reclaim it with a free-space optical analog Ising machine built from off-the-shelf components in which every spin is addressed in parallel and read out in a single camera shot, while letting the system evolve under analog dynamics rather than being written and read one spin at a time. We demonstrate this architecture with over 100,000 spins, the largest spatially multiplexed analog Ising machine reported to date, with a realistic path beyond one million spins limited only by spatial-light-modulator and camera resolution. Across sparse and dense MaxCut and fully connected number-partitioning instances, our machine matches state-of-the-art solution quality. Because every spin updates in parallel, throughput increases with system size, unlike time-multiplexed machines, which slow as problems grow. The same free-space geometry also lets us solve more than 50 problem instances simultaneously, further boosting throughput. Together, these results mark an important step towards a scalable, and energy-efficient Ising machine.

papers.title: Multipair-resilient entanglement swapping with complementary linear-optical measurements
papers.abstract: Multipair emission is a principal source of false heralds in entanglement swapping with spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources. A conventional Bell-state measurement (BSM) cannot distinguish the desired arrival of one photon from each neighboring source from a mixed-polarization double emission by one source accompanied by vacuum from the other. We show that a cascaded network can resolve this ambiguity by allowing its successive swapping stations to perform different measurements. A direct-basis BSM rejects same-polarization double emissions, whereas a balanced equatorial analyzer, implemented by a four-mode Green Machine (GM), uses two-photon interference to reject mixed-polarization double emissions. At the same time, it recovers same-polarization inter-source events rejected by the BSM as resolved $φ$-type Bell heralds. Their rejection sets jointly cover both single-source two-photon classes while retaining contributions from both useful inter-source classes. We classify the passive four-mode, number-resolving analyzers satisfying this condition and identify the BSM and GM as canonical balanced representatives. Using a Gaussian-state analysis exact to all orders of multipair emission, we evaluate three-source BSM--GM and four-source BSM--GM--BSM Pure Bell Pair sources under coupling, detector, and channel loss. The three-source network suppresses the leading infidelity, while the four-source network heralds an exact Bell state in the lossless limit, a property that holds for every alternating BSM--GM chain with four or more sources. The fidelity advantage over source-count-matched all-BSM networks persists at every loss level studied, a single-channel rate advantage appears without multiplexing, and spectral multiplexing raises the Bell-pair delivery probability toward the asymptotically deterministic limit.

papers.title: Hamiltonian Two-Way Coupling of Nonlinear Waves and 3D Flows
papers.abstract: Simulating large-scale free-surface water by coupling a localized 3D fluid solver to a cheaper 2D surface model has long faced a mismatch in wave dynamics: efficient 2D wave models used in graphics are typically either linear or non-dispersive. These models are fast, simple, and accurate for calm, small-amplitude seas, but coupling them with strongly nonlinear 3D solvers produces visible reflections and artifacts at the 2D--3D interface. We address this problem by introducing a nonlinear and dispersive 2D wave model based on the canonical Zakharov formulation. Its Hamiltonian structure, in which the surface elevation and surface potential form a canonical pair ($η$, $ψ$) governed by the wave energy, enables a canonically consistent two-way coupling scheme, allowing information to pass smoothly across the 2D--3D interface. Our 2D solver reduces mean wave-height error by 1.7--5$\times$ over SWE, BEM, and Airy baselines while running more than $10^3\times$ faster than BEM; it achieves greater nonlinear accuracy and coupling fidelity than SWE and Airy, with minor losses in speed and stability. Coupling it with a 3D Navier--Stokes solver yields a full system that suppresses visible seam artifacts across a range of experiments, including dispersion-matching and Kelvin-wake tests, and runs over 4$\times$ faster than a pure GPU NB-FLIP simulation on the same domain.

papers.title: First-principles perturbative theory of anomalous scaling in a stochastic shell model of turbulence
papers.abstract: Deriving anomalous scaling exponents from the equations of motion remains a central problem in the statistical theory of turbulence. Here we obtain a first-principles perturbative solution for a nonlinear stochastic dyadic shell model. The model preserves the conservative cascade structure and exact scaling symmetry of the deterministic dynamics, while stochastic transfer fluctuations provide a perturbative setting in which the leading-order rescaled dynamics is Gaussian. Using the statistically restored hidden scaling symmetry of the inertial-range equations, we determine the stationary statistics of the rescaled variables. We then formulate anomalous scaling as a Perron--Frobenius eigenvalue problem for the multiplier statistics. The resulting perturbative expansion yields explicit analytical expressions for the scaling exponents of structure functions of arbitrary order in the weak-noise regime. Direct numerical simulations provide an independent verification of the theoretical predictions. The results demonstrate that the hidden-symmetry perturbation framework extends from linear random models to a genuinely nonlinear cascade system.

papers.title: Wing-Rotor Aerodynamic Interactions in Small UAVs During Hover and Cruise
papers.abstract: A compact vertical take-off and landing aircraft requires the same tilt-rotor configuration to perform two fundamentally different aerodynamic tasks: sustain hover and deliver efficient cruise. This work investigates the underlying wing-rotor interactions in both operating regimes using a validated unsteady Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes equations-based computational framework. For cruise, the advance ratio governs the balance between thrust production, propulsive efficiency, and wake coherence. Lower advance ratios produce a tightly wound slipstream that undergoes strong vortex interactions, leapfrogging, and early wake bifurcation. At higher advance ratios, the slipstream retains a narrower and more coherent jet-like structure, improving propulsive efficiency while reducing both thrust of the propellor and lift of the wing. The flow impingement at the wing is characterized through the approaching, interaction, and convection phases, revealing the combined influence of vortex stretching, wake bifurcation, blockage, image-induced velocity, and streamwise momentum convection on the downstream wake. In hover, the propeller's rotational speed governs the overall aerodynamic performance more strongly than the wing's placement. Although the position of the wing with respect to the propellor modifies the local wake interactions and flow impingement on its leading edge, its influence on the integrated thrust coefficient and figure of merit remains limited. We also explain the vortex and wake dynamics around the propellor and the wing responsible for governing these aerodynamic performance.

papers.title: First-Principles Prediction of Nonlinear Optical Response in TiO$_2$ for High-Power Dielectric Mirror Applications
papers.abstract: Dielectric multilayer mirrors are essential components in optical experiments using high-power lasers, where titanium dioxide (TiO$_2$) is widely employed as a high-refractive-index dielectric material. In this study, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of TiO$_2$ under intense ultrashort laser pulses using real-time first-principles electron-dynamics simulations based on time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT). We reveal intensity-dependent absorption driven by multiphoton excitation and optically excited free carriers, and simulate the resulting electron-light coupled dynamics in TiO$_2$ nanofilms using a multiscale Maxwell-TDDFT framework. Direct evaluation of the reflected and transmitted fields shows reduced reflectance at high intensities ($I \sim 10^{13}$ W/cm$^2$), demonstrating a pronounced nonlinear optical response. Furthermore, the optical response properties are compared among various stable and metastable crystalline phases of TiO$_2$-rutile, anatase, brookite, TiO$_2$-II, and TiO$_2$-B-as well as an amorphous supercell model. These results provide microscopic insight into intensity-dependent optical degradation in TiO$_2$-based dielectric optical components exposed to intense femtosecond laser fields.

papers.title: Finite-domain inverse reconstruction of a Morris--Thorne-type wormhole candidate with a derivative-consistent $f(R)$ curvature sector
papers.abstract: We present a finite-domain inverse reconstruction of a Morris--Thorne-type wormhole candidate as a methodological benchmark for constrained numerical model building in modified gravity. The throat condition and local flare-out behaviour are embedded analytically in the shape-function parameterization, while the redshift profile is kept finite by construction. Rather than fitting $f(R)$, $f_R(R)$, and $f_{RR}(R)$ as independent numerical arrays, a positive analytic generator is assigned to $f_{RR}(R)$ and integrated to obtain a derivative-consistent reconstructed curvature sector. The frozen reconstruction is evaluated on 10,019 radial nodes over $r\in[1,10^{5}]$. The corresponding Ricci-scalar trajectory spans $-1.1317\times10^{-9}\leq R\leq1.999999998$ and is weakly non-monotonic, so no inversion $r=r(R)$ is required. On the same finite grid, the reconstructed source variables retain positive pointwise energy-condition margins, the coordinate-radial null-energy integrals are positive both globally and in the near-throat band, and the maximum normalized tidal-curvature ratio is $0.8666<1$. The reconstructed source-side closure diagnostic has a maximum absolute residual of $5.3246\times10^{-5}$. The source closure is phenomenological rather than derived from a unique microphysical matter Lagrangian or a uniquely specified curvature--matter coupling function. Accordingly, the result is not presented as a full field-equation solution of a specified nonminimally coupled $f(R)$ theory, a stability proof, an exterior-matched global spacetime, or an observer-dependent safe-traversal model. It instead provides a finite-domain computational benchmark for auditable inverse reconstruction of Morris--Thorne-type geometries in modified gravity.

papers.title: Carrier-Resolved Attosecond Valley Polarimetry of Monolayer MoS$_2$
papers.abstract: In recent years, all-optical writing and switching of valley polarization in two-dimensional semiconductors has been demonstrated on femtosecond timescales. Reading this polarization out on the same timescale, carrier by carrier, has so far remained out of reach. Employing semiconductor Bloch equation simulations of monolayer MoS$_2$, we show that attosecond transient absorption closes this gap by turning the Mo $4p$ semicore edge into a quantitative valley polarimeter. We find that pump-enabled core-to-valence absorption probes the holes while core-to-conduction bleaching probes the electrons, so that a single spectrum identifies each carrier by its photoabsorption energy. The hole channel, Pauli-blocked in equilibrium, emerges background-free. Its circular dichroism reverses sign with the pump helicity, and its normalized magnitude is proportional to the valley polarization. Finally, we show that scanning the probe delay clocks the few-femtosecond write in real time. Thus, attosecond core-level dichroism is a carrier-sensitive, quantitative probe of the creation and evolution of valley polarization.

papers.title: Single-Mode Control of High-Speed and Low-Threshold III-V/Si Quantum Dot Microring Lasers via Azimuthal Gratings
papers.abstract: Hybrid III-V/silicon quantum-dot microring lasers are compact, energy-efficient O-band sources, but their whispering-gallery cavities are inherently multimode and bidirectional, producing unstable mode hopping that is incompatible with dense wavelength-division multiplexing. We show that an azimuthal grating patterned into the silicon ring - a single lithographic degree of freedom - converts this multimode cavity into a wavelength-addressed, single-mode source. A coupled-mode analysis derives the angular-momentum selection rule from first principles and shows that the inner-wall corrugation replaces the degenerate counter-propagating pair with symmetric and anti-symmetric standing-wave supermodes of unequal radiative loss. At the second-order Bragg condition the anti-symmetric mode is symmetry-protected, yielding a high-quality-factor state at exactly one azimuthal order; finite-element simulations confirm this and identify grating depth as the primary loss-engineering handle. Devices fabricated in-house on a 100 mm silicon-on-insulator platform hold a single longitudinal order with a side-mode suppression ratio of 37.9 dB and continuous, hop-free tuning, while the emission wavelength stays fixed across a factor-of-two change in cavity loading, set lithographically rather than by the gain peak. Because the grating decouples the lasing wavelength from the quantum-dot gain, the detuning becomes a mask-level design variable that sets the temperature of minimum threshold current, reaching 1.95 mA near 50 °C. Combined with side-mode suppression beyond 37 dB and multi-gigahertz direct modulation, these lasers are practical building blocks for cascaded, wavelength-addressed transmitter arrays in data communication and co-packaged optics.

papers.title: The Hidden Second Law of Thermodynamics behind the Boltzmann-Grad Limit
papers.abstract: We show that the Boltzmann-Grad (BG) limit, $N\varepsilon^{d-1}=α=\text{const}$, is not a neutral scaling condition but already encodes the Second Law of Thermodynamics, resolving Loschmidt's paradox. Newton's First Law is the bridge: applying the BG condition locally to two adjacent cells at different temperatures, we decompose their evolution into a free-streaming period $δt_f$, governed by inertia alone, during which molecules cross the interface ballistically and still carry their cell of origin's velocity distribution; and a collisional adjustment period $δt_a$, governed by Newton's Second Law, during which the locally mixed, non-Gaussian population relaxes toward a new Gaussian equilibrium. Using the one-dimensional Gaussian velocity distribution, we show that isotropy alone produces non-zero net molecular and momentum flux across the interface, directed from the warmer to the cooler cell -- the microscopic origin of the pressure gradient driving the system toward uniformity. Treating relaxation as a sum of random collisional increments, the Central Limit Theorem fixes the collision count $n^*$ required for convergence, giving $δt_a \sim n^*\,\ell/\bar v$. This decomposition resolves Loschmidt's paradox: his reversal acts on a fixed, identifiable set of molecules, while the temperature field Boltzmann's equation tracks is carried by an ever-changing local population; the step relating the two -- convergence under the Central Limit Theorem -- is itself a coarse-graining that discards microscopic information by construction, recoverable only at an unavoidable thermodynamic cost, by Landauer's principle. Temporal irreversibility is present from the moment the BG framework, and the coarse-graining it requires, are adopted -- not generated during derivation.

papers.title: Ice melting in an oscillatory flow
papers.abstract: We investigate the melting dynamics of an ice disk subjected to an external oscillatory flow using two-dimensional direct numerical simulations, in the absence of buoyancy, varying the flow amplitude and its oscillation frequency. We identify two distinct regimes governed by the interplay between advection and diffusion within the boundary layer. For slow oscillations, the melting process is well described by an effective steady flow, where a description based on classical forced convection is applicable. For fast oscillations the melting time increases significantly and approaches the diffusion limit regime, as a result of the oscillatory flow being unable to renew the fluid within the oscillating boundary layer, causing cold meltwater to accumulate near the interface and reducing heat transfer.

papers.title: Predicting THz Generation Capability of Organic Crystals through Data Mining and Crystal Nonlinearity Models
papers.abstract: We report the use of DFT computation and mathematical models to predict the nonlinear dielectric polarization (P^{NL}) and nonlinear susceptibility coefficients (χ^{(2)}_{IJK}) of organic materials based on their crystal structures. We apply this computation approach on single-component crystals, co-crystals and ionic crystals found through data mining the Cambridge Structural Database. We verify these computational results with experimental terahertz (THz) generation efficiencies for known THz generators, demonstrating consistency between the measurements and the computed values. Several mined structures show similar or larger PNL values compared to state-of-the-art THz generation crystals DAST, OH1 and BNA, suggesting great potential for their use in nonlinear optical (NLO) applications. Importantly, we also compared the resulting model of nonlinear optical tensor components with commonly-used simplifications of nonlinearity, showing that the comprehensive approach should be the standard method to evaluate the nonlinear optical properties of single-crystalline materials.

papers.title: High-harmonic fingerprints of sharp spin twists in a chiral soliton lattice
papers.abstract: A magnetic field applied perpendicular to the helical axis of a monoaxial chiral helimagnet compresses the spin helix into a coplanar chiral soliton lattice (CSL). We show that optically driven high-harmonic generation from itinerant electrons coupled to a frozen CSL resolves the lattice-scale structure of the localized twist, rather than the continuum soliton shape. High-order harmonics remain perturbative for the uniform helix. As the winding localizes at fixed magnetic period, they grow by many orders of magnitude and acquire a nonperturbative dependence on the drive amplitude. The growth originates from a spatially nonuniform effective hopping that turns each soliton into a localized dip in the hopping amplitude. When the degree of winding localization is held fixed, high-order intensities fall by many orders of magnitude as the magnetic period increases toward the continuum limit, where the hopping modulation is spatially smoothed. High-order harmonics thus resolve a real-space characteristic of the coplanar CSL, even in the absence of scalar chirality and an emergent magnetic field.

papers.title: Effects of pressure on the chemical sooting structure of equi-diffusive counterflow diffusion flames
papers.abstract: The effects of pressure on the chemical sooting structure of equi-diffusive soot formation (SF) in a counterflow diffusion flame (CDF) are explored in a combined experimental and numerical study over pressures ranging from 1 bar to 6 bar. Experiments preserve the diffusive flame structure and carbon flux at increasing pressures and utilize measurements of soot concentrations, dispersion exponents and soot production rates. Numerical simulations are completed in OpenSMOKE++ with detailed \ce{C1}-\ce{C16} chemistry, lumped PAH consideration up to \ce{C160}, sectional soot model and tracking of the C/H ratio in particulates. Network-based tools are utilized to study the organization and evolution of carbon routing pathways. Results show that for equi-diffusive flames, soot concentration increases with residence time and pressure, whereas soot production rates are influenced only by pressure. Soot C/H ratio is observed to increase with pressure using numerical and experimental methods, but numerical solutions underestimate the increase in hydrogen abstraction reactions. The soot-forming network undergoes a percolation-like organization of its pathways before soot inception. The network then continues to grow by adding connections through its influential nodes. Acetylene is identified as a highly influential node in the carbon transfer graph, with its influence increasing with pressure.

papers.title: Effects of Quantum Noise and Source Blurring on Dark-Field Signal Retrieval in X-ray Speckle-Based Imaging
papers.abstract: X-ray speckle-based dark-field imaging offers high sensitivity to sub-pixel structural features, yet its quantitative reliability in clinical and preclinical settings remains constrained by low photon flux and finite focal spot sizes. However, how hardware-induced noise and source blurring propagate through retrieval algorithms to degrade signal integrity is not fully understood. Here, we systematically evaluate algorithm robustness quantified by signal linearity, sensitivity, and bias under photon starvation and source blurring across two mathematically distinct frameworks: differential-based intrinsic tracking (Low-Coherence System, LCS) and patch-wise explicit tracking (X-ray Speckle-Tracking Speckle-Vector-Tracking, XST-XSVT). Our experimental results demonstrate that input speckle pattern distortions propagate through retrieval algorithms in fundamentally different ways depending on algorithm architecture. As an example, using our setup, under severe photon starvation, derivative noise amplification in LCS causes its dark-field signal linearity and sensitivity to drop precipitously, while sharply elevating baseline bias. In contrast, XST-XSVT restricts these losses for sensitivity while maintaining a stable baseline, as its patch-wise variance calculation inherently suppresses stochastic noise. Similarly, under blur-limited conditions , source blurring washes out the speckle pattern, directly reducing dark-field sensitivity for both LCS and XST-XSVT. This characterization establishes operational boundaries for low-power and low-coherence X-ray systems, guiding algorithm selection and framework optimization to realize quantitative dark-field imaging in preclinical and clinical applications.

papers.title: Ultrafast tuning of the focusing efficiency of a nonlinear atomically thin lens
papers.abstract: Control over light focusing is paramount for optical and imaging systems. However, its implementation in active and integrated nanophotonic devices is hindered by the bulky and static nature of standard lenses. Here, we show that Fresnel Zone Plate Lenses (FZPL) based on a monolayer Transitional Metal Dichalcogenide are a viable solution to the challenges of miniaturization, integration, and active control of the focusing efficiency, featuring both ultrafast and large modulation depth. Using a monolayer $WSe_2$ FZPL, we demonstrate all-optical ultrafast ($\sim$ ps) modulation of the focusing efficiency close to $\sim$30\%, that we achieve by exploiting the nonlinear exciton-resonant enhancement and modulation of second harmonic generation.

papers.title: Phoretic interactions in two-medium wedge geometries
papers.abstract: We investigate the diffusiophoretic motion of a chemically isotropic active colloid in a three-dimensional wedge formed by two distinct fluid media, in the limit of vanishing Péclet and Reynolds numbers. The concentration field is obtained using the Fourier-Kontorovich-Lebedev transform, yielding an exact representation for arbitrary wedge opening angles and interfacial contrasts. We introduce the interfacial parameter $Γ=(1-λ\ell)/(1+λ\ell)$, where $λ$ denotes the diffusivity contrast and $\ell$ the solute partition coefficient. For $Γ=\pm1$ and commensurate wedge angles, the solution reduces to finite image constructions, with distinct structures for even and odd commensurability. The general solution also recovers the planar-interface and semi-infinite-interface limits. The leading-order translational phoretic velocity is derived from the concentration field, revealing a strong interplay between wedge geometry and interfacial properties that governs both the magnitude and direction of particle motion. This work provides a framework for understanding and controlling phoretic transport in confined multiphase environments and offer a basis for extensions to finite-size geometries and mixed fluid--fluid and solid boundary conditions. Our results may find applications in the control of active-particle transport in confined multiphase environments, where interfacial properties and geometry can be exploited to tune phoretic motion.

papers.title: Phase-controlled super-modes in a `lossy' tri-waveguide coupled micro-ring resonator system
papers.abstract: In coupled micro-ring resonator (MRR) systems, the coupling process plays a critical role in determining the optical response, yet models of these structures typically assume this process to be either lossless, or dissipative with either purely real or purely imaginary coupling rate, respectively. Dissipative coupling is contingent on having appropriately phase engineered structures with intricate coupling geometries, but systems exhibiting `lossy coupling', i.e., characterized by complex-valued coupling rates, have received comparatively little attention. In this work, we investigate the effect of such `lossy' coupling, by modelling the optical response of a tri-waveguide coupled MRR system, using Temporal Coupled-Mode Theory (TCMT). The `lossy' coupling occurs via a common bus waveguide, positioned between a pair of MRRs, leading to the emergence of a pair of intrinsic resonances, whose frequency and linewidth may be tailored by controlling the respective coupling rates from either MRR. We develop these ideas, and by connecting the input (driving) waveguides, using a 3dB y-splitter, demonstrate a novel, coherently driven, lossy-coupled MRR, which exhibits either an absorptive or transparent resonance peak on demand by phase-controlled super-modes.

papers.title: AlGaAs nanowires as a universal platform for GaAs, InGaAs, and InAs quantum dots
papers.abstract: Optical quantum dots (QDs) are central to photonic quantum technologies, with fabrication approaches tailored to different spectral ranges. A key challenge, however, is the realization of a unified platform$\unicode{x2014}$a single growth method combined with a host material offering a designable architecture$\unicode{x2014}$enabling wavelength tunability across the full emission range and co-integration of multiple quantum dots. Here, we introduce AlGaAs nanowires as a universal host for GaAs, InGaAs, and InAs QDs. Building on our previous demonstration of high-quality GaAs QDs, we realize InGaAs QDs with tunable emission by varying the growth duration from 2 to 5 s, achieving emission at 780 and 920 nm. We further showcase the platform's versatility for multi-quantum-dot devices by co-integrating two InGaAs QDs, as well as GaAs and InGaAs QDs within a single nanowire. Finally, we initiate a first step toward pure InAs QDs by growing a pristine InAs segment on AlGaAs nanowires, demonstrating material compatibility.

papers.title: Feedback control of vortex shedding using data-driven modelling
papers.abstract: This paper details the data-driven modelling and feedback control of vortex shedding past a circular cylinder at a Reynolds number of Re = 1000. We study the effect of varying the order of the reduced model for control design purposes and demonstrate that higher orders can lead to lower suppression of vortex shedding. We use the Bode integral theorem and a frequency-domain interpretation to show that this drop in performance is, in part, due to the classical ``waterbed effect'', which increases sensitivity in frequency bands of unmodelled dynamics. Training data from 2D unsteady simulation is used to obtain linear reduced-order state-space models of the system via dynamic mode decomposition with control. Using only lift measurement, we show that at least a 4th-order model is required for an LQG controller to suppress vortex shedding, with the best performance achieved with as few as 9 modes, whilst higher-order (>14) controllers show a significant decrease in performance. We study the influence of external disturbances, noise rejection, and parameter uncertainty on controller performance. A 28.6 dB reduction in lift coefficient variance is achieved, resulting in a 26% reduction in drag. We further show that, for control design purposes with practical actuation bandwidth, the closed-loop control delivers a significant 13.7% drag reduction within 3D DDES, despite having been trained with 2D URANS and therefore argue that 2D URANS simulation is sufficient for reduced-order model generation and control design.

papers.title: Remarks on Fixed- and Variable-Order Fractional-Laplacian Closures for TurbulentDissipation
papers.abstract: Two independent attempts, separated by two decades, to encode turbulent dissipation with a fractional Laplacian both converge on the operator order as the signature of the fully developedinertial range: the additive, fixed order model, and the dynamically deforming operator of the Adaptive Fractional Navier Stokes. We show that, despite sharing this fixed point, the two constructions belongto distinct universality classes: Chen operator is a superposition of two fixed order kernels whose relative weight drifts with scale, while AFNS posits a single operator whose order itself flows continuously with the local Reynolds number. We derive a scale resolved observable, the effective spectral order, whose logarithmic anomaly term discriminates between these two mechanisms in principle, and then obtain a sharper, purely analytic verdict from the two dimensional, enstrophy conserving limit: the generative mechanism matching a stable process index to the empirical pair dispersion law has no solution once vortex stretching is kinematically switched off. Whether this dichotomy leaves a residual signature in real quasi two dimensional flows is left as an open experimental challenge.

papers.title: Quantum Vibronic Dynamics Shape Catalytically Relevant Au-Ligand Interfaces in Atomically Precise Gold Nanoclusters
papers.abstract: Atomically precise gold nanoclusters are versatile for photocatalysis and energy conversion because their electronic structure stems from strong metal-ligand interactions. However, these interactions are mostly discussed statically, leaving dynamic reorganization of Au-ligand interfaces under photoexcitation unclear. We investigate rod-shaped [Au25(PPh3)10(SC2H5)5Cl2]2+ using ultrafast transient-grating spectroscopy, two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy, ab initio calculations, and hierarchical equations-of-motion simulations. The multidimensional spectra resolve multiple electronic relaxation pathways and a hierarchy of coherent structural motions, from localized Au-ligand distortions to collective framework vibrations. Wavelet analysis reveals that high-frequency Au-ligand vibrations emerge immediately after excitation, whereas low-frequency collective modes appear later through interstate vibronic coupling, indicating sequential redistribution of structural coherence. Simulations reproduce the nonlinear response and identify the microscopic vibronic couplings responsible. The results show that photoexcitation drives continuous ultrafast reorganization of the Au-ligand bonding network, transiently reshaping interfacial electronic structure before thermalization. This work establishes dynamic Au-ligand interfaces as the microscopic link between excited-state energy flow and photochemical function in atomically precise nanoclusters.

papers.title: Nonlocal-nonlinear phonon polaritons
papers.abstract: When light is confined to deeply subwavelength volumes, optical responses can become nonlocal. Yet how nonlocality reshapes nonlinear light-matter interactions remains largely unexplored, particularly in dielectrics. Here, we theoretically uncover a new class of nonlinear optical processes arising from the interplay between optical-phonon propagation and ionic-bond anharmonicity in polar crystals. We show that, unlike conventional local nonlinearities, this mechanism enables second-order responses even in centrosymmetric materials. Moreover, these responses can be tuned by the confinement and resonantly enhanced near optical-phonon resonances. Using density functional perturbation theory, we quantify the resulting nonlocal second-order susceptibilities in representative polar crystals. Our results establish nonlocal-nonlinear optics as a new regime of light-matter interaction in dielectrics.

papers.title: Assessment of turbulent fire dynamics and combustion instabilities using a flamelet model
papers.abstract: The Sandia one-meter methane fire plume is an established benchmark for turbulent combustion modeling of large-scale flames. This study investigates the combustion instabilities formed close to the base of the Sandia fire plume. Finite rate chemistry and differential diffusion are considered using a flamelet/progress variable (FPV) approach. The performance of the FPV approach is assessed by comparing with the eddy dissipation model (EDM) and the experimental data for the large-scale fire plume via large eddy simulations (LES). The effects of radiation modeling and mesh resolution on the predictive capability of the model are systematically investigated by comparing the axial and radical velocities against the experimental data at various locations. Although all models successfully capture the primary flow characteristics of fire plumes, the FPV model with differential diffusion yields improved predictions in the near-flame-base region. The formation mechanism of cellular flow structures near the flame base is investigated via a budget analysis of the vorticity equation, and the type of instability governing the formation of the cellular structure is clarified. Finally, the individual effects of finite rate chemistry and differential diffusion on the prediction of the thermo-chemical quantities are quantified. Overall, this study explains the underlying physics governing combustion instabilities at the base of turbulent fire plumes, provides novel insights into the performance of flamelet models for LES of gaseous pool fires, and offers reliable guidance for the high-fidelity numerical simulation of large-scale turbulent buoyancy driven flames.

papers.title: Quantum-optimal instruments for high-contrast imaging with multi-plane light converters
